text:
incident-bot: PAGED: [SLO] tail-latency spike detected for customer blueleaf — p99 > 6s, streaming stalls reported. auto-notify oncall.

amanda: grabbing this — oncall-sre. seeing alerts for p95 ~1.2s -> 1.8s and p99 ~2.6s -> 6.3s across a small subset of hosts. alert rule: infra/latency/tail/customer-blueleaf

amanda: quick check — is this single-tenant? metrics tag shows tenant=blueleaf and route=/v1/chat/stream

sophia: support here — blueleaf on call says some users reported stalled responses mid-stream ~10:20 UTC. They also attached a very long prompt template (10k chars) used in batch job.

raj: eng-runtime — possible KV-cache miss / OOM on kv shards when someone hits long context + concurrency. checking runtime logs for stall traces.

infra-bot: deployed new kernel-optimized runtime to pool-3 at 10:05 UTC — no errors reported in deploy. Autoscaler scaled up 2 GPUs at 10:17 UTC due to CPU pressure.

amanda: ok running `curl` against metrics: top-hosts by p99 show host-7 and host-9 spike. connections count for blueleaf on those hosts = 460 concurrent streams. normal is ~40.

kevin: cs/solutions — Blueleaf started a nightly ingestion that changed requests from short prompts to one-shot long prompt per user, concurrency high. they replicated it to prod last night.

raj: grabbing flamegraphs, also pulling trace for a stalled stream. here's truncated stack from host-7:
```
2026-03-14T10:18:02Z runtime: stream stalled at kv_cache_lookup
goroutine 1421: waiting on kv-lock
... quantize_kernel: memcopy fallback
```

raj: looks like long prompts blow up sequence length, KV cache thrash, and combined with high concurrency we hit mem pressure -> long GC/lock waits -> streaming stalls & tail latency. Also see repeated model fallback events to quantized variant.

amanda: impact: blueleaf requests account for ~82% of p99 increase. Other tenants unaffected. Current mitigation options:
- throttle blueleaf concurrency (rate-limit per api-key)
- route blueleaf to dedicated lower-concurrency pool
- temporarily disable streaming for blueleaf -> fall back to non-streaming generation
- enable aggressive prefix/KV caching for repeated prompt prefixes

sophia: suggested to contact Blueleaf and ask to pause ingestion job while we mitigate. they already acknowledged and are willing to pause for 30 min.

raj: immediate plan: 1) apply per-tenant concurrency cap 2) enable prefix caching 3) spin up 2 smaller dedicated instances and migrate a fraction of Blueleaf traffic 4) keep streaming on but set stream-chunk-timeout to 1s

amanda: executing 1) now: adding temporary quota via rate-limiter:
```
POST /admin/quotas
{ "api_key": "blueleaf-prod", "concurrency": 60 }
```

amanda: quota applied. seeing connection count drop from 460 -> 58 on host-7 over 90s. p99 trending down.

raj: enabling prefix caching config for customer tag blueleaf: `enable_prefix_cache=true, cache_ttl=600s`

infra-bot: cache config pushed to runtime pool-3 and pool-9 at 10:27 UTC.

kevin: Blueleaf confirms ingestion paused at 10:25 UTC.

amanda: spinning up two dedicated small instances (dedicated-4g) and adding routing rule to route 25% traffic for blueleaf there for canary.

infra-bot: autoscaler launched 2 dedicated-4g instances at 10:29 UTC. routing rule add scheduled.

raj: migrating canary subset now — route test traffic -> dedicated-4g. initial latency p99 on canary ~1.1s. good signal.

amanda: p95/p99 for blueleaf overall: p95=0.9s, p99=1.6s at 10:35 UTC. still above SLO of p99<=1s but much improved.

sophia: thanks team. Blueleaf asking for ETA to full recovery and root cause.

raj: root cause summary (short): unusual one-shot long prompts + sudden high concurrency from ingestion job => KV cache thrash + memory pressure in runtime leading to lock contention and streaming stalls. mitigation: concurrency cap, prefix caching, customer routing to dedicated instances, and they paused ingestion.

amanda: handoff time — I need to go offline for a scheduled call at 11:00. handing to raj for continuing monitoring and postmortem. tagging oncall-rotation: @raj you're the responder.

raj: ack. I'll keep monitoring 30m, gather traces and logs, and start a postmortem doc. preliminary action items:
- infra: evaluate kv cache eviction strategy and per-tenant memory isolation (kevin)
- runtime: add stream stall detection and early backpressure signal (raj)
- product: consider per-tenant burst limits / automated dedicated routing when sustained concurrency detected (liam)
- support: follow up with Blueleaf on ingestion job and recommend chunking prompts (sophia)

liam: product acked — we'll draft limits and doc for recommended prompt sizes and streaming best practices.

amanda: leaving this thread. current status: incident mitigated, customer paused ingestion; p99 trending to ~1s. still on raj to finish writeup.

raj: will create postmortem link and notify stakeholders. adding timeline + metric charts. reopening if regressions occur.

sophia: thanks all :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: auto-clear after 11:05 UTC — final p99 for blueleaf at 10:55 UTC = 0.98s. incident duration ~45m.
